title: SP9-101: Touchscreen and pen need the out-of-tree ITHC driver (no upstream driver for the ADL THC in legacy mode)
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | P1 | touch | missing-driver | broken | works | broken |

## Problem

On a stock kernel the SP9 touchscreen and Slim Pen 2 do not work at all. The touch controller is the
Alder Lake-P Touch Host Controller (PCI 8086:51d0), which only the downstream `ithc` driver
(linux-surface 0006, quo/ithc-linux) drives. With ITHC but without iptsd, touch is single-touch only.

## Origin

Intel never upstreamed THC support for Alder Lake. Intel's `intel-thc-hid` (QuickSPI/QuickI2C, mainline
since 6.14, Even Xu) only claims Meteor Lake and newer. The SP9 runs its THC in legacy mode
("no ACPI config, using legacy mode", seen in #2367), which `intel-thc-hid` does not implement. quo,
who wrote ITHC, will not submit it under a pseudonym (quo/ithc-linux#7), and nobody else has posted it.
No IPTS or ITHC patch has ever reached linux-input (patchwork search, 2026-11-14).

## Reports

- [linux-surface discussion 2282](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/discussions/2282) (discussion) "Collecting scattered SP9 fixes for upstreaming, links welcome": single touch without iptsd
- [linux-surface#1330](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1330) (closed issue, user-setup) "surface pro 9 touchscreen and pen not working": SP9 touch and pen dead: iptsd missing
- [linux-surface#1848](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1848) (closed issue, user-setup) "surface pro 9 - pen not working, no /dev/ipts/ directory": SP9 pen dead: no /dev/ipts (UAPI moved to hidraw)
- [linux-surface#1156](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1156) (closed issue, user-setup) "Pen from Surface pro 9 under Fedora 38 install?": Fedora 38 SP9 pen needs linux-surface kernel plus iptsd
- [linux-surface#818](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/818) (open issue, sibling) "SP8 touchscreen and pen support": SP8 touch and pen support history
- [quo/ithc-linux#34](https://github.com/quo/ithc-linux/issues/34) (open) "No touch input on Surface Laptop 5 (Alder Lake, 8086:51d0): device created but zero events, even with poll=1": SL5 (same 8086:51d0) gets zero events on Fedora 44
- [intel/thc-drivers#1](https://github.com/intel/thc-drivers/issues/1) (open) "Multi-touch not working on Surface Laptop 7 with Intel THC driver": Intel's out-of-tree THC drivers, Surface report unanswered

## Fixes, patches and PRs

- [quo/ithc-linux#7](https://github.com/quo/ithc-linux/issues/7) (open) "Rolling into the kernel?": upstreaming tracker, open since 2022
- [quo/ithc-linux#29](https://github.com/quo/ithc-linux/issues/29) (open) "Official Intel QuickSPI Linux driver": Intel QuickSPI driver: ADL QuickSPI easy, legacy mode needs ithc-legacy.c merged
- [quo/ithc-linux#33](https://github.com/quo/ithc-linux/issues/33) (open) "Improve error recovery, locking, and shutdown behavior (PR)": PR: error recovery and locking; quo's review sets the bar for an upstream version
- [linux-surface/kernel#132](https://github.com/linux-surface/kernel/issues/132) (closed PR, superseded-pr) "HID based IPTS and ITHC support": HID based IPTS and ITHC support in linux-surface (downstream, 2022)
- [patchwork.kernel.org/project/linux-input/list/?series=909501](https://patchwork.kernel.org/project/linux-input/list/?series=909501): Intel THC drivers v2 (Even Xu), mainline 6.14, MTL and newer only

## Possible solutions

- Short term on stock Fedora: build quo/ithc-linux out of tree and sign it with a MOK, as John-S-Reddick/bazzite-surface does; package it as an akmod/kmod (RPM Fusion or Terra) until it is upstream.
- Long term option A: someone carries ITHC to linux-input as a HID transport driver after the cleanup quo listed (kernel style, error handling, full re-init on error).
- Long term option B: merge ITHC's legacy mode into Intel's intel-thc-hid and add the ADL PCI IDs; ask Even Xu and Xinpeng Sun (Intel) whether they would take it.

## Next steps

- [ ] Ask quo whether he would accept someone else submitting ITHC or the legacy-mode merge with his authorship (quo/ithc-linux#7).
- [ ] Ask Intel (Even Xu) on linux-input whether legacy-mode THC (ADL, TGL) is welcome in intel-thc-hid.

- Upstream target: linux-input (Jiri Kosina, Benjamin Tissoires), Intel THC maintainers (Even Xu, Xinpeng Sun)
- People: quo, StollD, Even Xu

body:

## Problem

Multitouch and pen on the SP9 need the iptsd daemon. Fedora does not ship it; users take it from the
linux-surface repo or Terra.

## Origin

Nobody filed a Fedora package review (Red Hat Bugzilla search, 2026-11-14). Repology lists iptsd only in
AUR, nixpkgs, Solus and Terra. Every build dependency is already in Fedora rawhide: cli11-devel,
eigen3-devel 5.0.1 (the version iptsd's wrap pins), fmt-devel, inih-cpp, guidelines-support-library-devel,
spdlog-devel; the optional tools need sdl2-compat and cairomm. No bundling is needed.

## Reports

- [linux-surface discussion 2282](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/discussions/2282) (discussion) "Collecting scattered SP9 fixes for upstreaming, links welcome": iptsd has to come from a third-party repo

title: SP9-103: Touch and pen stop working after suspend/resume
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | P1 | touch | bug | n/a | partial | broken |

## Problem

After s2idle resume the touchscreen and pen sometimes stay dead until iptsd or the ITHC module is
restarted. It is the most repeated unsolved touch problem across the linux-surface trackers.

## Origin

Suspected: ITHC tears down and recreates the hid_device on suspend, and iptsd holding the old hidraw
node can deadlock or keep a dead handle (quo, quo/ithc-linux#20; linux-surface#2210 patch description).
Firefox-only loss of touch after sleep (#1402) looks like a separate userspace problem.

## Reports

- [linux-surface#1171](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1171) (closed issue, stale) "Touch and pen stopped working after resume from sleep": touch and pen dead after resume; mentions quo's DMA fix b51f328 (closed not planned)
- [linux-surface/iptsd#122](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/122) (closed issue, stale) "Touch and pen stop working after sleep": touch and pen stop after sleep (closed not planned)
- [linux-surface#1799](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1799) (closed issue, stale) "[SP10] Dead touchscreen on arch 6.15 kernel": SP10 dead touchscreen after resume (closed without fix)
- [sebanc/brunch#2202](https://github.com/sebanc/brunch/issues/2202) (closed) "Multi touch and pen don't work after sleep mode on Surface Pro 9": SP9 multitouch and pen dead after sleep
- [linux-surface#273](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/273) (open issue, workaround) "Touchscreen stops working after Resume": touch after resume on older devices; quo explains hidraw recreation
- [linux-surface#1402](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1402) (open issue, workaround) "Firefox does not detect touch input after sleep": SP9: only Firefox loses touch after sleep
- [quo/ithc-linux#20](https://github.com/quo/ithc-linux/issues/20) (closed) "Touch screen not working after suspend": SP8 touch after suspend; quo switched to full shutdown and reinit on suspend

## Fixes, patches and PRs

- [linux-surface#2210](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2210) (closed PR, promised-never-resubmitted) "Add Linux 7.0 patch series for Surface Pro 9": closed PR carrying 'ithc: Fix PM suspend/resume to preserve hid_device across s2idle' (author never resubmitted)

## Possible solutions

- Test the orphaned #2210 patch on the SP9 with an rtcwake loop; if it holds, offer it to quo/ithc-linux with the author's agreement.
- Workaround: restart iptsd from a systemd sleep hook after resume.

title: SP9-104: ITHC fails to initialise on some boots or units (EFI stub DMA error, legacy init -110)
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| needs-test | P2 | touch | bug | n/a | partial | n/a |

## Problem

Two failure modes are reported on the SP9: with the kernel booted as an EFI stub, ITHC reports
"invalid dma rx data" and touch never starts; on one unit `ithc_legacy_init` times out with -110 on every
boot and touch has never worked. A third report: touch locks up while the magnetic charger is attached.

## Origin

EFI stub: quo found bit 5 of THC register 0x1128 set only on working boots and committed 18afc6f
(2024-04, "hopefully fixed"). Legacy init -110 (UEFI 22.107.143, 7.2.15): unknown, no maintainer reply.
Charger lock-up: unknown.

- [linux-surface#1078](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1078) (open issue, could-close) "[SP9] Touchscreen not working with efi stub kernel": SP9 touch dead when booted as EFI stub (still open)

title: SP9-105: iptsd service and udev rule are fragile (stops after cold boot, probes every hidraw, loses its tag)
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fix-pending | P1 | touch | bug | n/a | partial | n/a |

## Problem

iptsd@.service can stop itself about 6 s after a cold boot; the udev rule runs iptsd-check-device on every
hidraw node, which can stall input for seconds or lock the user out at the lock screen; a udev change
event drops the systemd tag so the service loses its device; raw ITHC input nodes duplicate iptsd's events.

## Origin

`StopWhenUnneeded=yes` in the unit, an udev rule matching `ACTION=="add"` only, and a probe that is not
limited to ITHC/IPTS devices. All have small fixes posted as PRs with no maintainer reply.

## Reports

- [linux-surface/iptsd#228](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/228) (open issue, patch-pending) "iptsd-check-device causes 6s bus timeout on AMD Surface Laptop 4 SPI touchscreen": iptsd-check-device causes 6 s bus timeout on AMD SL4 SPI touchscreen
- [linux-surface/iptsd#229](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/229) (open issue, patch-pending) "udev rule probes every hidraw node, including USB HID; a blocking probe": udev rule probes every hidraw node incl. USB; blocking probe locks out the lock screen
- [linux-surface/iptsd#163](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/163) (open issue, patch-pending) "iptsd@.service unit file loses access to the ipts device unit service": service loses access to the device after a change event
- [linux-surface/iptsd#220](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/220) (open issue, patch-pending) "udev: Ignore raw Intel Touch Host Controller input nodes to prevent dupl": duplicate raw ITHC input nodes and 16:9 distortion
- [linux-surface#2299](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2299) (open issue, workaround) "ipts: controller fails to resume with -EAGAIN after a short suspend": IPTS resume -EAGAIN leaves iptsd unkillable (OnFailure= recovery)

## Fixes, patches and PRs

- [linux-surface/iptsd#219](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/219) (open PR, waiting) "iptsd@.service stops itself ~6s after start on cold boot due to StopWhenUnneeded": remove StopWhenUnneeded=yes (service stops ~6 s after cold boot)
- [linux-surface/iptsd#221](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/221) (open PR, waiting) "udev: hide raw ithc input nodes duplicated by iptsd": hide raw ITHC input nodes
- [linux-surface/iptsd#224](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/224) (open PR, waiting) "udev: Keep the systemd tag across change events": keep the systemd tag across change events

## Possible solutions

- Review and test the three PRs on the SP9; ask the iptsd maintainer (StollD) to merge; carry them in the Fedora package meanwhile.
- Restrict the udev probe to known THC/IPTS hidraw parents.

## Next steps

- [ ] Test #219, #221 and #224 together on the SP9 and post Tested-by on each PR.

title: SP9-106: Erratic touch detection and weak palm rejection with default iptsd settings
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fix-pending | P2 | touch | bug | n/a | partial | n/a |

## Problem

Taps need force, swipes break, palms register while writing, and DisableOnStylus leaves some touches or
splits gestures. The linux-surface wiki carries an SP9 calibration override as a workaround.

## Origin

Contact detection defaults changed in iptsd dd0c322 and are too strict for several devices; a contact
missed for a single frame ends the touch; DisableOnStylus has edge cases.

- [linux-surface/iptsd#235](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/235) (open PR, new) "Skip detection on frames below the deactivation threshold. Merges cleanly.": skip detection below the deactivation threshold

## Problem

Fast pen strokes come out jagged; measured pen event rate on the SP9 is about 66 Hz.

## Origin

iptsd only emits a position for some DFT window types. An SP9 user processes position on every DFT window
(Position, MPP2 position, pressure and an unknown type) and reaches about 266 to 300 Hz.

title: SP9-111: libwacom has no SP9 tablet description (pen and touch not recognised as a tablet)
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | P2 | pen | upstreaming | n/a | works | broken |

## Problem

GNOME and Plasma tablet settings, pen mapping and palm-rejection grouping need a libwacom entry. Upstream
libwacom has none for the SP9; libwacom-surface (fork) has one but conflicts with Fedora's libwacom, which
Plasma requires.

## Origin

iptsd creates uinput devices on BUS_VIRTUAL. Upstream libwacom only accepts usb, serial, bluetooth and i2c
(its UINPUT_SUBSYSTEM override maps only to those). Two attempts to add the MEI bus were refused: Peter
Hutterer will not support buses that only exist with out-of-tree kernel code (libwacom#92, #93 in 2019;
#400 in 2021). Newer Surfaces on intel-thc-hid will show up on SPI, which libwacom does not know either.

## Reports

- [linux-surface discussion 2282](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/discussions/2282) (discussion) "Collecting scattered SP9 fixes for upstreaming, links welcome": swapping libwacom for libwacom-surface plus an override file works
- [linux-surface/libwacom-surface#13](https://github.com/linux-surface/libwacom-surface/issues/13) (closed issue, fixed-package) "Missing Pro 8 support": SP9 data added in the fork
- [linux-surface/iptsd#212](https://github.com/linux-surface/iptsd/issues/212) (closed) "libwacom-surface removes a lot of fedora 44 kde plasma packages": libwacom-surface removes many Fedora 44 KDE packages
- [linuxwacom/libwacom#89](https://github.com/linuxwacom/libwacom/issues/89) (closed) "Microsoft Surface IPTS device integration": Microsoft Surface IPTS device integration (mass-closed 2022)
- [rhbz#2463712](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2463712) (CLOSED/ERRATA) "gnome-shell crashes on startup: libwacom assertion bus_to_str on Microsoft Surface (i2c-hid touch/pen)": libwacom bus_to_str abort on a Surface (fixed 2.18.0-2)

## Fixes, patches and PRs

- [linuxwacom/libwacom#92](https://github.com/linuxwacom/libwacom/issues/92) (closed-unmerged) "Add support for Intel Management Engine bus": MEI bus support (closed by author after maintainer concerns)
- [linuxwacom/libwacom#93](https://github.com/linuxwacom/libwacom/issues/93) (closed-unmerged) "Device data for IPTS based Microsoft Surface Devices": IPTS Surface device data (closed)
- [linuxwacom/libwacom#400](https://github.com/linuxwacom/libwacom/issues/400) (closed-unmerged) "Adds Intel Management Engine Interface (MEI) Bus": MEI bus, second attempt (closed for no reply)
- [linuxwacom/libwacom#967](https://github.com/linuxwacom/libwacom/issues/967) (closed) "Switch tablet dimensions from inches to mm": tablet dimensions in mm (affects the fork's SP9 file)
- [linuxwacom/wacom-hid-descriptors#490](https://github.com/linuxwacom/wacom-hid-descriptors/issues/490) (open) "Contributing: MS Surface Pro 9": SP9 sysinfo contributed

## Possible solutions

- Ask Peter Hutterer once how IPTS/ITHC (virtual) and THC QuickSPI (SPI) Surfaces should be described; options: iptsd tags its uinput devices with UINPUT_DEVICE/UINPUT_SUBSYSTEM, or libwacom gains virtual/spi buses.
- Then send the SP9 data file (Stylus=true, Styli list, size in mm).
- Workaround now: the /etc/libwacom override plus the udev LIBINPUT_DEVICE_GROUP rule (docs/workarounds.md).

## Next steps

- [ ] Open a libwacom issue asking the bus question, linking the earlier refusals.

title: SP9-201: Type Cover does not work at the LUKS passphrase prompt (dracut lacks surface_aggregator_hub)
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | P1 | cover | upstreaming | works | works | broken |

## Problem

With an encrypted root, the Type Cover keyboard is dead at the LUKS prompt on Fedora, so the disk cannot
be unlocked without a USB keyboard.

## Origin

The cover keyboard and touchpad are children of the SAM KIP hub, bound by `surface_aggregator_hub`.
dracut master already installs `=drivers/hid` (surface_hid, surface_hid_core), `=drivers/tty/serial`
(8250_dw, 8250_lpss), `=drivers/pinctrl`, `intel_lpss_pci` and `surface_aggregator_registry` in the default
(sloppy) hostonly mode, but not `surface_aggregator_hub` (read 2026-11-14, dracut 04e04cfe). A second cause,
the SAM probe race, is SP9-202.

## Reports

- [linux-surface#1221](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1221) (open issue, patch-pending) "[SP9] Start Fedora 38 LUKS with Surface Pro Signature Keyboard [SOLVED]": SP9 Fedora 38 LUKS with Signature Keyboard (solved with modules)

- [omacom/omarchy#14195](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/14195) (open) "Fix AMD Surface keyboard support at the LUKS prompt": Omarchy LUKS keyboard module list

title: SP9-202: Type Cover dead or slow after boot: SAM probe returns -EINVAL before the pin controller is ready
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fix-pending | P1 | cover | bug | partial | works | partial |

## Problem

Sometimes the cover keyboard and touchpad do not work after boot (or only after reattaching or a
suspend cycle). Discussion 2282 reports the cover taking a moment to start after attaching.

## Origin

When surface_aggregator probes before pinctrl_tigerlake has bound the wakeup GPIO, ssam_irq_setup()
returns -EINVAL instead of -EPROBE_DEFER, so the probe is never retried. Wu Enqiang's v2 fix is accepted
in platform-driver-x86 and should reach 7.5 and stable.

## Reports

- [linux-surface#2219](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2219) (open issue, patch-pending) "surface_serial_hub: probe fails with -EINVAL instead of -EPROBE_DEFER when the wakeup GPIO is not ready": surface_serial_hub -EINVAL instead of -EPROBE_DEFER (confirmed on SP9)
- [linux-surface#1645](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1645) (closed issue, config) "[SP9[NixOS] Keyboard&Trackpad not working after upgrade to 6.12.4": SP9 NixOS keyboard dead after 6.12.4 until pinctrl_tigerlake loaded first
- [linux-surface#1651](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/1651) (open issue, needs-info) "Keyboard and touchpad are unresponsive sometime on boot and after session": SP9 keyboard and touchpad sometimes dead at boot or after resume
- [linux-surface#2064](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2064) (open issue, unsolved) "Keyboard not always available after boot": keyboard not always available after boot
- [linux-surface discussion 2282](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/discussions/2282) (discussion) "Collecting scattered SP9 fixes for upstreaming, links welcome": cover takes a moment after attaching

## Fixes, patches and PRs

- [lore:20261024054921.48209-1-janussss@163.com](https://lore.kernel.org/r/20261024054921.48209-1-janussss@163.com) (platform-driver-x86, changes-requested/accepted, Wu Enqiang, 2026-10-24) "[v2] surface: aggregator: propagate -EPROBE_DEFER from ssam_irq_setup()": Wu Enqiang v2, accepted in platform-driver-x86

title: SP9-206: Rotation and light sensor hang in iio-sensor-proxy (claims time out, rotation freezes)
body:
| Status | Priority | Area | Kind | Mainline | linux-surface | Fedora |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| open | P1 | sensors | bug | partial | partial | broken |

## Problem

With iio-sensor-proxy 3.6+ (Fedora ships 3.9) the SP9 accelerometer and light sensor claims time out,
screen rotation freezes and `systemctl stop iio-sensor-proxy` hangs.

## Origin

The SAM sensor hub (045E:005D) reports accel and light only on change (in_accel_hysteresis 0.05, light 1 /
relative 20) and surface_hid cannot fetch input reports on request, so every sysfs raw read waits 5 s when
the tablet is still. iio-sensor-proxy 3.6+ polls these sensors on its main thread.

## Reports

- [linux-surface#2160](https://github.com/linux-surface/linux-surface/issues/2160) (open issue, workaround) "iio-sensor-proxy not working - Surface Laptop Studio (1st gen)": iio-sensor-proxy not working (SLS); CmdrShepardsPie's SP9 analysis and udev rule
